category_title: Students who engage in disruptive behavior to avoid difficult academic tasks
minimal_context: David is presented with a reading assignment during his English Language Arts class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: David, it is time for ELA. Please read this passage and complete the assignment at your desk.

STUDENT: (Stares at the paper) I'm not reading this. It's too long.

TUTOR: You need to do your work. Just get started.

STUDENT: (Pushes the assignment off the desk) No! I'm not doing it.

TUTOR: David, pick up your paper right now or I will have to send you to the office.

STUDENT: I don't give a s***! Send me to the office, I'm not doing this f***ing reading!

options.A: Teach the student to use a self-monitoring form, having him check the appropriate box at the end of ELA, math, and science, and turn it in for verification.
options.B: Adjust the ratio of lower-level to higher-level reading questions based on the student's level, keeping the percentage of lower-level questions highest for struggling readers across subjects.
options.C: Establish a classroom reading community founded on respect for choice and individual perspectives to support the student's engagement during the ELA, math, and science periods.
options.D: Allow the student to choose his own creative reading projects based on his strengths and interests to complete independently during the ELA, math, and science periods.
